title: User-Defined Aggregate Functions
description: Create custom aggregate functions using state transition functions and finalizers with CREATE AGGREGATE.

data.text: PostgreSQL allows developers to construct custom aggregate functions by defining a **State Transition Function** (accumulates values row-by-row) and an optional **Final Function** (transforms the accumulated state into the final result).

data.title: Creating a Geometric Mean Aggregate
data.content: Building an aggregate using exp() and avg(ln()).

data.text: `CREATE AGGREGATE` needs a state transition function and an optional finalizer. The transition function receives the accumulated state and the next input value and returns the new state. The finalizer turns the final state into the result. This is how PostgreSQL implements built-ins such as `avg` and `sum` internally.

data.title: A geometric mean aggregate
data.content: The transition accumulates the sum of logarithms; the finalizer exponentiates the average to produce the geometric mean.

data.title: Interview angle: aggregates are just state machines
data.text: Once you see an aggregate as a state transition plus an optional finalizer, ordered-set aggregates such as percentile and `mode()` stop being mysterious. Interviewers sometimes ask how `avg` or a median would be implemented; answering with a transition function, a state type, and a finalizer shows that you understand the execution model rather than just the syntax.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `CREATE AGGREGATE` combines state transition and finalizer functions.
State is preserved in an accumulator (`STYPE`) across all evaluated rows.
Custom aggregates integrate natively with `GROUP BY` and window `OVER` clauses.
